title: Notes from New York
excerpt: Field notes from four winters shooting the city after midnight — where the light pools, and which streets stay honest.
intro: New York After Dark took four winters. These are the working notes — the corners that kept giving, and the hours when the city finally stops performing.

body.text: Between 2 and 5 am the city becomes a different instrument. The avenues empty, the sodium light pools on wet asphalt, and the people you do meet have nowhere left to hurry to. I worked almost exclusively between 23rd and 14th streets, west side, where the grid tilts just enough to hold reflections.

The technical notes are boring, which is the point: a fast prime, a high tolerance for grain, and no tripod. A tripod is a claim on territory; a camera at chest height is a conversation. The moment you set up a tripod on a New York sidewalk, the photograph you came for leaves.
